title: Seven-Round Forward and Six-Round Inverse Integral Distinguishers for Alzette
summary: Bit-based division-property search reaches six forward and five inverse rounds, but whether stronger methods yield the next-round integral distinguishers remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For the Alzette ARX-box, the reported bit-based division-property search found a $6$-round forward integral characteristic but no $7$-round forward integral distinguisher, and a $5$-round inverse integral characteristic but no $6$-round inverse integral distinguisher. These negative results are limited to that search and do not establish that such distinguishers are impossible in general. Determine whether any $7$-round forward or $6$-round inverse integral distinguisher exists, either by extending the bit-based division-property search to longer characteristics or by applying a stronger method.

scope.domain: Integral and automated cryptanalysis of the Alzette ARX-box.
parameters: Round count and direction: six versus seven forward rounds and five versus six inverse rounds
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether any seven-round forward or six-round inverse integral distinguisher exists, either by extending the bit-based division-property search to longer characteristics or by applying a stronger method.

progress.summary: The source reports six-round forward and five-round inverse integral characteristics from a bit-based division-property search, but no corresponding next-round distinguishers. It presents these negative findings as limited to that search and leaves the broader existence question open.
